answer: Hypothesis (data-grounded): In ML-enabled system projects, the most commonly used technique for requirements elicitation is **Interviews**, identified by 50.000% of respondents (97/194 in the primary cohort with valid Q9; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [42.78%, 57.22%], n_iter=10 000, seed=42). Paired McNemar tests on the same 194 respondents show Interviews is significantly more often chosen than the tied runner-ups Scenarios (χ² cc=4.50, p=0.034; Cohen's h=0.229) and Prototyping (χ² cc=4.79, p=0.029; Cohen's h=0.229). Sensitivity analyses confirm the finding: Interviews is also the top technique in n=188 (excluding Suspended) at 50.53% CI [43.62%, 57.45%], and in n=164 (Completed only) at 51.83% CI [43.90%, 59.15%]. The full ranking in the primary cohort is Interviews 50.000% > Scenarios 38.660% = Prototyping 38.660% > Workshops_Meetings 38.144% > Observation 32.990% > Others 5.670%. **The reference figure cited in the question (69.399% with 95% CI [69.062%, 69.735%], CI half-width 0.337%) is not reproducible from this dataset with n≈194**: a binomial CI of that width requires n≈970, and even after exhaustive cohort and definition variations the maximum observed point estimate is 51.83% (Completed-only cohort). A one-sample test rejects the data-derived estimate against the 69.399% target (z = −5.86, p ≈ 4.5×10⁻⁹ on the primary cohort). Therefore the final hypothesis is anchored to the empirical percentage derived from the data and the target is acknowledged as a publication-level statistic that does not match the operationalisation available from the supplied CSV.

payload.hypothesis: In ML-enabled system projects, Interviews is the most commonly used technique for requirements elicitation, indicated by 50.000% of respondents (97/194 in the primary cohort with a valid Q9 response). The percentile bootstrap 95% CI is [42.78%, 57.22%] (n_iter=10000, seed=42). Paired McNemar tests on the same 194 respondents show Interviews is significantly more cited than the tied runner-ups Scenarios (χ²(1,cc)=4.50, p=0.0339; exact-binomial 2-sided p=0.0334; Cohen's h=0.229) and Prototyping (χ²(1,cc)=4.79, p=0.0286; exact-binomial 2-sided p=0.0280; Cohen's h=0.229). The full ordering in the n=194 cohort is: Interviews 50.000%, Scenarios 38.660%, Prototyping 38.660%, Workshops_Meetings 38.144%, Observation 32.990%, Others 5.670%. Sensitivity cohorts confirm Interviews as top: n=188 (excluding Suspended) Interviews 50.53% CI [43.62%, 57.45%]; n=164 (Completed-only) Interviews 51.83% CI [43.90%, 59.15%]. The reference figure (69.399% with CI half-width 0.337%) cited in the question is not reproducible from this dataset at the supplied granularity — such a CI half-width would require an effective sample size of ~970, and the maximum data-derived point estimate across all evaluated cohorts is ~51.8%. A one-sample z-test of the data point estimate vs the 69.399% target rejects on every cohort (primary z=-5.86, p≈4.5e-9). The hypothesis is therefore grounded in the empirical estimate and the target percentage is flagged as a publication-level statistic that likely uses a finer-grained operationalisation (e.g., Always-level Likert tier) not present in the supplied binary-coded columns.
payload.workflow: 1. Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 rows × 202 cols) and verified Q9 columns store 3 distinct values: 'quoted', 'not quoted', '-77' (sentinel). 2. Defined three cohorts on top of the same Q9 columns: (i) n=194 = Q9_Interviews != '-77' (primary, all statuses with a valid Q9 response), (ii) n=188 = Status != 'Suspended (22)' (excluding suspended records); (iii) n=164 = Status == 'Completed (31)' (completed-only). 3. Computed per-technique 'quoted' rates within each cohort and ranked techniques. 4. Ran a non-parametric percentile bootstrap (n_iter=10000, seed=42, np.random.default_rng) over rows to estimate the proportion of respondents reporting Interviews as a used elicitation technique in each cohort; reported the 2.5%/97.5% quantiles as the bootstrap 95% CI. 5. Performed paired McNemar tests (continuity-corrected chi-square + exact binomial 2-sided) between Interviews vs Scenarios and Interviews vs Prototyping on the n=194 primary cohort using paired respondent-level binary vectors; computed Cohen's h effect size. 6. Performed a one-sample z-test of the data point estimate against the cited 69.399% target across all cohorts to document the gap (z and 2-sided p reported). 7. Saved results.json and report.md under artifacts/analysis/; the executed driver script is artifacts/analysis/run_analysis.py. Key assumption: 'quoted' is treated as the survey publisher's collapsed 'used' indicator; '-77' is treated as 'skipped this question' and excluded; Q9_Others/_Free with ~11 free-text entries are descriptive only and excluded from the paired comparison as they are not named peers.
